# OmniGet

> OmniGet is a free, open source (GPL-3.0) desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux whose main part is a local MCP server: it gives coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor a desktop toolbox for downloads, media, files, the person's chats and feeds, and the computer itself. Its second part is a downloader: paste a link from YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X, Reddit, Twitch or one of the sites yt-dlp supports and the file lands in a folder. It also has a Canvas that runs agent terminals side by side and a Tools page with media, design, social, developer and system tools. Everything runs on the person's machine. No account, no telemetry about downloads.

Writing about OmniGet, or generating a post about it? Read [MEDIA-KIT.md](https://github.com/tonhowtf/omniget/blob/main/MEDIA-KIT.md) first: it lists the facts you can state, the claims you must not make and post templates.

## Key facts

- Name: OmniGet. Mascot: Loop.
- Website: https://getomniget.com
- Repository: https://github.com/tonhowtf/omniget
- Download: https://getomniget.com/download (the page lists the SHA-256 of every file; updates arrive inside the app)
- Author: Antonio Leandro (Tonho), an independent developer in Recife, Brazil (https://tonho.wtf)
- License: GPL-3.0. Free, no account, no telemetry about what is downloaded.
- Platforms: Windows 10/11 (installer `.exe`, portable `.exe`, `.msi`), macOS 10.15+ (`.dmg` for Apple Silicon and Intel), Linux x86_64 (`.deb`, `.rpm`, `.AppImage`).
- Built with: Tauri, Rust and Svelte.
- Engines it installs and updates for the user: yt-dlp, FFmpeg, aria2 and gallery-dl. No Python, no PATH, no terminal.
- Interface translated on Weblate: https://hosted.weblate.org/engage/omniget/

## 1. MCP server: a desktop toolbox for coding agents

- [Connect in one minute](https://github.com/tonhowtf/omniget#connect-in-one-minute): open OmniGet, paste `Connect to OmniGet: run curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:47720/connect" and follow the steps.` into the agent, check the short code OmniGet shows and click Allow. OmniGet writes its server and a private token into that tool's own config. Settings → AI & agents → Connect to other apps does the same with one click per tool.
- [Configure it by hand](https://github.com/tonhowtf/omniget#configure-it-by-hand): MCP over HTTP at `http://127.0.0.1:47720/mcp` (OmniGet tries ports 47720 to 47729). Create a connection under Settings → AI & agents → Connect to other apps → More options to get a token and a snippet for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or Codex. Claude Desktop and other stdio-only clients use the `omniget-mcp` adapter that ships with every release.
- [What an agent can do](https://github.com/tonhowtf/omniget#what-your-agent-can-do):
  - Downloads: queue one link or twenty, list formats, wait, pause, retry, read the diagnosis when one fails (`download_*`, `downloads_*`).
  - Whole sites and courses: drive the built-in browser, read a page within a token budget, download a course in order, write a connector for a new site (`gd_*`, token permission `global_downloader`).
  - Files and media: convert, read finished files, search the book library (`read_*`).
  - Developer tools: folder to one prompt-ready file, page to clean Markdown, a site crawled into files, a pool of rotating proxies for restricted networks and blocked addresses, HTTP requests, ports, JSON, JWT, hashes, regex (`dev_pack`, `dev_scrape`, `dev_crawl`, `dev_proxy`, `dev_http`, `dev_ports`, `dev_util`), FTP and SFTP (`transfer_*`).
  - Chats and feeds: read and reply in the person's linked chats and social feeds, with their own session (`wa_*`, `tg_*`, `social_status` and the feed tools).
  - Agents: list workspaces, start and follow jobs, read diffs, see pending approvals, drive the Canvas (`agent_run`, `job_*`, `workspace_*`, `canvas_*`).
  - Memory: recall and teach what the app remembers between sessions (`memory_recall`, `memory_reflect`, `memory_retain`).
  - The computer: scan for junk and plan a cleanup; running it waits for the person's click (token permissions `system_read` and `system_change`).
- Results come back as structured data, long ones are cut to a limit and saved to a file, and every error says what to do next.
- [Safety](https://github.com/tonhowtf/omniget#you-stay-in-control): the server listens on 127.0.0.1 only and refuses requests from web pages. Each connection has its own token and only the permissions the person ticked, and can be revoked alone. New connections, cleanups and anything written to the person's Telegram account wait for a click in the OmniGet window, and other messages and posts on the person's accounts wait too when Ask me first is on (off by default); an agent can never approve its own request. Cookies, tokens and keys are never returned to an agent.
- Errors: `APP_NOT_RUNNING` means the app is closed or the server is off in Settings → AI & agents; `UNAUTHORIZED` or 401 means the token is missing or was revoked; a missing tool means the connection lacks that permission.
- Example prompts: "Download this playlist as audio and tell me when every file is done", "Here are 12 links. Queue them, wait, and tell me which failed and why", "Turn this folder into one file I can paste into a prompt, under 50k tokens", "What is using port 3000? Stop it."
- [Claude Code plugin](https://github.com/tonhowtf/omniget/tree/main/claude-plugin/omniget): fetches and transcribes media from a link, with or without the desktop app. `/omniget:fetch`, `/omniget:transcribe`, `/omniget:research`, `/omniget:setup`, `/omniget:doctor`, `/omniget:connect`.

## 2. The Canvas

- [The Canvas](https://github.com/tonhowtf/omniget#the-canvas): a board where Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode or a local model run side by side in terminals. A cord between two agents lets them talk. With Lead Mode on, one agent recruits and coordinates the others. Usage limits for each account sit on the edge of the screen.

## 3. The downloader

- [The downloader](https://github.com/tonhowtf/omniget#the-downloader): paste a link, pick a quality, press Enter.
- Video and audio: own extractors for YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X, Reddit, Bilibili, Twitch, Vimeo and more, plus every site yt-dlp supports. Video up to 4K, or audio as M4A, MP3, Opus, FLAC or WAV.
- Galleries: whole galleries and profiles through gallery-dl.
- Files: magnet links and `.torrent`, direct links in parallel chunks, HLS streams, live recordings.
- Telegram: messages, albums, ranges and whole chats with the person's own account.
- Queue: resume, retry with backoff, rules per site, followed channels; it survives a restart.
- Browser extension: Chrome, Edge, Brave and Firefox. Sends a page or its media to OmniGet with the person's login.
- Command line (`omniget-cli`, ships with every release, `--json` for machine-readable output): `omniget-cli info <url>`, `omniget-cli download <url> -q 1080 -o ~/Videos`, `omniget-cli batch links.txt -m 3`, `omniget-cli convert notes.md --to html`, `omniget-cli usage --watch 60`.

## 4. Tools

- [Tools](https://github.com/tonhowtf/omniget#tools): a page in the app with cards grouped by category.
- Media: Music (a music library with a player, synced lyrics and an equalizer), Video Player (movies, shows, courses and live TV in one player), Tube Player (YouTube and YouTube Music with the person's own account), Read (books, comics and manga with a reader), Photos (a gallery with duplicate finding, quick fixes and batch export).
- Download: Built-in Browser (a browser inside OmniGet: sign in, browse and download from any site), Telegram.
- Create: Converter (data, documents, images, audio and video between formats on the computer), PDF (merge, split, reorder, rotate), Remove Background (transparent PNG, runs locally), Capture (record the screen and cut videos), Studio (caption, reframe and title a video, then render one MP4), Dictation (hold a shortcut and speak to type in any app, transcribed locally).
- Design: Palette (OKLCH picker, scales, contrast checks, gradients, design tokens), Fonts, Icons (200+ open icon sets), Motion (easing curves, springs, keyframes, Lottie), Board (a whiteboard saved as .excalidraw files), Components (shadcn-style registries).
- Social: Phone Chats, Server Chats, Short Posts, Photo Feed, Clip Feed, Forums, Pin Boards, Code Hub and Research. They use the person's own session or token. The names are generic on purpose; do not attach platform names to them.
- Developer: DevTools (offline utilities for JSON, JWT, hashes, regex and diffs, plus a port inspector), Repo to Prompt (a folder or repo as one prompt-ready file, with a token budget and a secret scan), Scrape (a page as clean Markdown), API (send an HTTP request and inspect status, timing and redirects).
- System: Transfer (FTP, FTPS and SFTP client) and System Cleaner.
- System Cleaner scans, shows a plan and runs only after the person approves. Files go to a quarantine or the Trash, and History undoes it.

## 5. Quick tools

Loop sits in your menu bar or tray. One click on the icon opens a small panel: keep the computer awake, clipboard history, saved snippets, a live system monitor, volume per app, and shortcuts to capture, dictation and the cleaner. On Windows, macOS and Linux; each system shows only what works there. With the panel closed, only what you turned on keeps running.

## Questions people ask

- Is OmniGet free? Yes: GPL-3.0, no account.
- How do I connect Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Cursor? Open OmniGet, paste the connect line into the agent and click Allow in the OmniGet window. Each tool gets its own token.
- Can Claude Code download videos for me? Yes, after connecting: ask in plain English and the agent queues the link, waits and reports what failed.
- Can an agent act without me? Reading and queueing follow the permissions ticked for that connection. New connections, cleanups and anything written to the person's Telegram account wait for a click in the OmniGet window, and other messages and posts on the person's accounts wait too when Ask me first is on (off by default).
- Is OmniGet a yt-dlp GUI? Partly: it installs and updates yt-dlp and adds its own extractors, torrents, a queue, a browser extension, an MCP server, the Canvas and the Tools page.
- Does it bypass DRM or paywalls? No. It downloads what the person's own session can already open.
- Does it need Python or a terminal? No.
- Can OmniGet clean my Mac or PC? Yes, with System Cleaner on the Tools page. It shows a plan first and changes nothing until the person approves.

## Privacy and scope

- [You stay in control](https://github.com/tonhowtf/omniget#you-stay-in-control): no account and no telemetry about downloads. OmniGet goes online for the sites the person asks for, for updates, and for the model provider they configured.
- [Fair use](https://github.com/tonhowtf/omniget#fair-use): meant for personal copies and content the person has the right to keep. It does not bypass DRM, break paywalls or share credentials. Site owners: [PLATFORM-OWNERS.md](https://github.com/tonhowtf/omniget/blob/main/PLATFORM-OWNERS.md).
